_meta.purpose: Curated, manually-maintained directory-name reference tables for the L12 native-vendored-dependency-inference job (design-v3.md §4.2/§4.2.1) -- specifically scripts/extract_vendor_candidates.py, but written as a standalone data file (same pattern as eol-reference.json) so other tooling that needs the same two lists (a future SBOM-merge step, a future syft-wrapper container per design-v3.md §4.2's Tier B container-expansion plan, etc.) can load it too instead of each carrying its own hardcoded copy.
_meta.coverage: Two independent lists. `system_libdir_prefixes` is near-universal (standard toolchain/OS library search paths on a Linux/glibc host) and was derived from a real observed link command (a stock Ubuntu clang++ link pulled in 80+ .pc files from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu alone -- see design-v3.md §4.2.1) -- extend it as other host distros/toolchains (musl, Windows/MSVC via -L for the Windows SDK and MSVC CRT/UCRT paths, macOS SDKs) are actually exercised, not speculatively. `in_tree_vendor_dirnames` is a heuristic naming convention list (directories that conventionally hold vendored/third-party code even when they're inside the repo) -- best-effort, non-exhaustive, and matched as a case-insensitive path-segment substring by extract_vendor_candidates.py, never a definitive classification on its own.
_meta.maintenance: Update this file by hand when a real run surfaces system noise not covered by system_libdir_prefixes, or a real vendored-code directory naming convention not covered by in_tree_vendor_dirnames. Both lists are informational strings consumed by extract_vendor_candidates.py's --libdir-reference flag; if this file is not passed, the script falls back to its own built-in defaults (kept in sync with this file's initial content) and says so.

system_libdir_prefixes.note: Standard Linux system library root; also covers /usr/lib/gcc/... (compiler-internal libgcc/libstdc++) since this is matched as a prefix, not an exact path.
RPM-based distro convention (RHEL/Fedora/openSUSE) for the 64-bit system library root.

Host-local installs outside the distro package manager -- still not a target-specific vendored dependency, but worth a second look if a candidate here has no obvious system-package origin (e.g. it's something the build host happened to have installed, not something the target ships).
Legacy/symlinked system library root (often a symlink to /usr/lib on modern distros, kept as its own prefix since not every host symlinks it).

in_tree_vendor_dirnames.note: Common but also a common name for a target's OWN library output/source directory -- expect more false positives from this entry than the others; confidence scoring in extract_vendor_candidates.py treats a bare directory-name match as weak evidence on its own.
